Subject: Fwd: Orchid questions — memory isolation and token economics

Team — forwarding Orchid's clarifications. Short notes below (internal):

- Quantization: if Orchid can't accept int8 on 32B, H100 (80GB) or A100-80GB are the only practical reserved choices without model surgery. But A100 has weaker fp16 throughput for long contexts vs H100 due to sparsity/kernels; H100 gives better perf for sustained decode throughput with large KV caches.

- L4 role: L4 is great for 13B and embeddings; it is cost-efficient for short-conv latency-sensitive traffic. For burst-only use, we should recommend L4 as a separate burst pool and avoid co-location with reserved H100 nodes that host 32B KV caches to reduce noisy-neighbor memory pressure.

- Isolation: recommend soft isolation with node-affinity + cgroup-level GPU memory limiting + request routing. For Private customers, we can provide dedicated GPU pools (no co-tenancy) or VPC-level isolation with strict scheduling.

- Token economics: from the worksheet, estimated token cost (reserved) per 1M tokens: H100 reserved: ~$170, A100 reserved: ~$210 (higher ops cost because more instances), L4 burst (spot-like): ~$45 for 13B workloads (but not suitable for 32B). Exact depends on concurrency and batching.

Proposed reply: give a concrete reserve/burst plan, cost compare per 1M tokens, and ops notes on isolation + an optional A100 pilot for customers who want an intermediate memory/perf tradeoff.

Ben
"Note: numbers in worksheet assume 256-token average context for 13B, 1,024 tokens for 32B long-context runs."

Hi Maya —

Appreciate the clarity. Below is a compact plan that balances predictability + cost while honoring the no-quantization requirement for your 32B model.

Proposed Tiering (reserved + burst):
- Reserved pool: (H100-80GB) x 8 nodes — dedicated to 32B family (supports model weights + KV cache; targets 95% of long-context traffic).
- Reserved fallback: (A100-80GB) x 2 nodes — reserved but lower priority; used during scheduled maintenance of H100 (acts as in-region fallback).
- Burst pool: (L4) x 12 nodes (config as preemptible/burst) — handles 13B and embedding traffic; autoscale up to 24 for short spikes.

Why this mix?
- H100 reserved: fits 32B without model surgery, delivers best throughput per GPU for long contexts due to tensor core kernel selection and HBM bandwidth.
- A100 reserved fallback: provides memory headroom if H100s are in maintenance and preserves reserved predictability where H100 capacity is constrained.
- L4 burst: cheap per-token for 13B short convs and embeddings; use a separate bursting fleet to avoid memory fragmentation on H100/A100 nodes.

Operational controls to mitigate interference:
- Strict routing rules: route 32B traffic only to H100/A100 reserved pools. 13B traffic tagged and routed to L4 burst unless explicitly pinned.
- KV cache pinning: reserve local NVMe for large KV-cache snapshots; do not mix KV-attach workloads on burst nodes.
- QoS and cgroups: enforce per-container GPU memory ceilings and CPU shares to avoid eviction cascades.
- Canary rollout policy: start with 70% reserved coverage for typical load, test failover to A100, then enable burst autoscaling for 2-week pilot.

Cost delta summary (back-of-envelope, see attached quote):
- H100 reserved baseline: ~$170 / 1M tokens (long-context workload)
- A100 reserved fallback: ~$210 / 1M tokens (less efficient for sustained long decode)
- L4 burst (13B workloads): ~$45 / 1M tokens when batched aggressively

Next steps:
1) Confirm KMS/keys and whether Orchid wants fully dedicated H100 racks (Private) or can accept Redwood Dedicated with single-tenant pools.
2) If dedicated racks needed, procurement lead time for H100 config is ~8–12 weeks; A100 ~6–8 weeks; L4 setup is ~2–3 weeks for burst pools.
3) We’ll schedule a 30-min ops runbook review with your SREs — propose Mon 9/6 9am PT.

If this looks good I’ll update the quote and seat the A100 fallback as an optional line-item.

Best,
Jasmine
